Hi Sofia / Mediware legal team,

Thanks for sending over the redlines. Attached is our internal summary and the two small documents we referenced (MSA redlines and the Order Form v3). High level areas we need to resolve before we can finalize:

- Governing law: Customer has proposed California. Our standard is Delaware for the MSA; we sometimes accept CA for order-specific agreements.
- Venue/arbitration: Customer requests arbitration in San Francisco. We prefer arbitration in Delaware / or JAMS in NYC for commercial disputes.
- Equitable relief carve-out: Mediware wants broad carve-outs for injunctive relief. We need to limit that to IP and data/security-related injunctive relief.

Can internal legal (Markus / Laura) weigh in on a compromise approach we can present that balances legal risk and deal velocity? Neha — commercial tension here on changing law/venue; your guidance on how far we should bend to close quickly would help.

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick note and the attachments. A few points from our side (Mediware counsel):

1) Governing law — Mediware is a California corporation with operations and contracts team based in SF; standard practice is to keep CA law for ease of enforcement and internal approvals. We can be flexible with forum selection if Redwood provides a reciprocal concession elsewhere.

2) Arbitration — customer prefers JAMS/AAA in San Francisco (or SF federal court on certain equitable claims). They will likely insist on neutral arbitrator language and a prohibition on venue-transfer clauses.

3) Equitable relief — Mediware will not agree to language that narrows injunctive relief too narrowly. Their position: in addition to IP and privacy, they want the ability to seek emergency relief for regulatory compliance and data retention issues.

I have attached a marked version with our comments. If Redwood can accept CA law and SF arbitration with a limited carve-out that still allows emergency regulatory relief, we should be able to move to signature quickly.

Jordan Ellis
Partner, Clyde & Partners LLP

Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form — jurisdiction/arbitration redlines (Mediware)

Team — reviewed Jordan's comments and Mediware’s redline. Proposed compromise below (redline text included inline for speed):

1) Governing law: For the Master Services Agreement (MSA) we should keep Delaware law. For the Order Form only (where billing and service-level specifics live) we can accept California law. Rationale: limits precedent exposure for general contract interpretation while giving commercial comfort on the order-specific items.

2) Arbitration / Venue: Accept arbitration with JAMS/AAA administered proceedings in San Francisco for disputes arising solely under the Order Form, subject to the following: (i) mutual selection of arbitrator if >$5M dispute, (ii) explicit waiver of class or representative actions, (iii) Redwood reserves right to seek injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction (see below).

3) Equitable relief carve-out (narrowed): Redwood will agree to an emergency injunctive relief carve-out limited to: (a) alleged infringement of Redwood's intellectual property; (b) unauthorized access or disclosure of customer data that creates immediate risk of material harm; and (c) regulatory orders that require immediate suspension or change to service delivery. Proposed clause (one paragraph):

"Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction solely to prevent immediate and irreparable harm relating to: (i) allegations of infringement of intellectual property; (ii) a material and demonstrable unauthorized access, disclosure, or loss of Customer Data; or (iii) a regulatory or governmental order that would require suspension or material modification of the Services. Any such request for temporary relief shall be limited to the minimum relief necessary and shall not be treated as a waiver of the agreement to arbitrate for other claims."

4) Class action waiver: keep firm — cannot accept class/collective relief.

Commercial input: if team is comfortable with CA law on the Order Form and SF arbitration limited as above, we can push that into the redline and circulate to Mediware for final check. If they insist on CA law for the MSA as well, escalate to execs.

-Markus
